- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.3) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If recent history shows strong downward trend + negative sentiment, model tends to overcorrect upward — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent low.  
- After a sharp spike in price, model often overshoots — apply a 3–5 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 2–4% per day post-spike.  
- When sentiment is positive but price is falling, model tends to ignore trend — adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true price.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below 70% of 30d mean, reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid mean-reversion miss.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings, model overestimates recovery — apply a 1–2% downward bias to forecast.
